name: Both accessors must each do their job (ID used to pair records, absences used to compare) vs. any one accessor call is enough
side_a: No_deduct only when the response's algorithm actually uses getStudentID to establish the history/math pairing AND uses getAbsences to compare the paired records' absence counts — i.e., both accessors appear in their distinct functional roles (ID-match condition guarding, or feeding, an absence comparison).
side_b: Deduct whenever the response's design collapses to a single role — comparing absences without ever matching students by ID, or matching students by ID without ever reading absences — even though the surviving accessor is called correctly and repeatedly on CourseRecord elements of both lists.

name: Wrong comparison/counting semantics tolerated vs. correct absence logic required for this sub-item
side_a: No_deduct for this sub-item when the accessor calls are present and correctly paired, even if the surrounding logic is wrong — e.g., using >= instead of >, counting students instead of summing extra absences, or breaking out of the inner loop after the first match.
side_b: Deduct whenever the absence comparison or the returned quantity is semantically incorrect, treating the faulty comparison as a failure to use getAbsences properly.

name: sole absences comparison is strict `>` vs. inclusive `>=` (ties counted)
side_a: no_deduct if the only absences-to-absences comparison the response makes is a strict greater-than (`>`), so equal absence counts are excluded
side_b: deduct if the response's only absences-to-absences comparison is inclusive (`>=`, or equivalently `<=`/`!<`), since counting ties does not establish that one student has MORE absences than the other — an inclusive operator alone never satisfies the item, no matter how correctly the records are paired

name: absence values are actually read and compared vs. only student IDs are compared
side_a: no_deduct if the response calls getAbsences() (or otherwise obtains absence counts) on records and compares those values to each other
side_b: deduct if the response never compares absence values — e.g., it only matches/compares student IDs or set membership and increments a counter on that basis — since no comparison of absences is performed anywhere

name: Correctness of the boolean test guarding the increment: any conditional counts vs the conditional must be the correct test (ID match + strict history > math)
side_a: Do not deduct based on what the conditional actually tests. As long as the increment sits inside some `if` inside a loop, award the point even if the test omits the student-ID match (`if (histRecord.getAbsences() > mathRecord.getAbsences())`), uses the wrong relational operator (`>=` instead of `>`), or never compares absences at all (`if (mathStudents.contains(cr.getStudentID()))`). Logic errors in the condition are graded under other sub-items, not this one.
side_b: Deduct unless the guarding conditional is the semantically correct one — i.e. it matches student IDs between the two lists AND strictly compares history absences greater than math absences — so that the counted quantity is genuinely 'students with more history than math absences'.

name: Shape of the enclosing loop: single pass with auxiliary structure counts vs nested traversal of both lists required
side_a: Do not deduct when the conditional increment lives in a single `for` loop over one list while the other list was preprocessed into a map/set (`HashSet<String> mathStudents`, `HashMap<String, Integer> mathAbsencesMap`); a loop containing the conditional increment is enough regardless of how the other collection is reached.
side_b: Deduct unless the increment is inside a conditional nested within loops that iterate both `historyList` and `mathList` directly.

name: Return value is a count of qualifying students vs. an accumulated absence-difference total
side_a: No deduct if the method increments a counter by exactly 1 for each matched student whose history absences exceed math absences, and returns that count.
side_b: Deduct if the method returns a different quantity than a student count — e.g. summing the numeric difference in absences (or otherwise adding more than 1 per student) — so the returned value is a total of absences rather than a number of students.

name: Counting is gated on an absences comparison vs. gated only on the student appearing in both lists
side_a: No deduct if the increment is guarded by a comparison of the two records' absence values (getAbsences() of the history record vs the math record).
side_b: Deduct if the increment happens on mere membership/ID match with no comparison of absence values at all, so every student enrolled in both courses is counted.
